<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **29** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/apps/connector-docusign/objectstack.manifest.json`, `packages/apps/connector-docusign/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/apps/connector-github/objectstack.manifest.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **39** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **181** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69e133ea0d9734dd0447d08875bbd8e3af0e1517` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e2e24b15b6ea88b503300b66f70205a9e40eaee0` — the merge of head `95b6e070942530efdf3f947b7f90e8d089fc9ea7` into base `69e133ea0d9734dd0447d08875bbd8e3af0e1517`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e2e24b15b6ea88b503300b66f70205a9e40eaee0 && git checkout e2e24b15b6ea88b503300b66f70205a9e40eaee0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 69e133ea0d9734dd0447d08875bbd8e3af0e1517 95b6e070942530efdf3f947b7f90e8d089fc9ea7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 69e133ea0d9734dd0447d08875bbd8e3af0e1517 && git merge --no-ff 95b6e070942530efdf3f947b7f90e8d089fc9ea7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69e133ea0d9734dd0447d08875bbd8e3af0e1517
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 69e133ea0d9734dd0447d08875bbd8e3af0e1517` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Reviewed read-only at 2026-11-06T18:41Z against the card's rulings (comments 6683195046 and 6691021157), the net diff `origin/main...95b6e07` (76 files), the cited code at the head, and the head's check-runs read once: 67 runs, 58 success, 9 skipped (Lint UI, Dogfood Verify CLI, UI Published Artifacts, the opt-in gates), 0 pending, 0 failure — nothing NOT MEASURED. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check UI`, `Test Core` and `Build Core` all green on this head. The dev's reports and the seat's conclusions were not used as evidence.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Enums and cardinalities — right.** `MarketplaceBusinessFunctionSchema` carries the ruling's F1 values in the ruling's order (sales, marketing, customer-service, finance, hr, supply-chain, administration, project, legal, it, collaboration); `MarketplaceIndustrySchema` the ten F2 values in order with no `general`/`cross-industry`; `MarketplaceSolutionTypeSchema` app | template | connector, no `theme`; `PackageMaturitySchema` beta | stable. `businessFunctions` is 1-3 distinct and order-preserving (taxonomy.zod.ts `distinct` + `.min(1)` + `.max(MAX_BUSINESS_FUNCTIONS)`), optional on Package / the two requests / TemplateManifest, required on MarketplaceListing — consistent with the ruling's "schema 层面字段可以不填 … 上架市场时至少 1 个". `industries` 0-3 distinct, optional everywhere. Row shapes default `solutionType: 'app'` and `maturity: 'stable'`; requests and the manifest carry no default, so a re-publish never rewrites a stored value (the `visibility` lesson, pinned in taxonomy.test.ts and the CLI test "sends no facet the manifest does not declare").
2. **`LEGACY_CATEGORY_MAPPING` — right against 3.1 and 3.2.** Every row of 3.1 (crm→[sales]+tag crm, erp→[finance, supply-chain]+tag erp, hr/finance/project/collaboration mapped, analytics/automation/ai/other manual with the ruled tags, integration manual+connector, security and developer-tools→[it] with tags, ui-theme and storage `unlistable` under ADR-0019) and of 3.2 (app/application/apps manual app; sales, marketing, productivity→[collaboration]; operations/business/ops→[administration] with `review: true` and tag operations; data manual + tag analytics; integrations/connector/connectors manual connector; devtools/tools/developer→[it]+tag devtools; utility and travel manual with their tag; starter manual template with `isStarter` untouched). No `other` bucket anywhere; a `manual` value is the author's choice (pinned: "folds nothing into a catch-all"). Two parts of 3.2 are migration-process rules a static table cannot hold and belong to cloud#3661: the `integrations` row's "read the manifest's original category first, then remap", and "unknown value → manual + the original value as a tag" (the table returns `undefined` for a value outside it — the right signal, but the migration must read it as manual, never as a skip). Should-fix, carried by cloud#3661, not this PR — see ③(d).
3. **Tombstones follow ADR-0087's registration — right.** Six `retiredKey()` sites on the authorable shapes plus `facets.categories` on the search response; six exact `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]` entries (`marketplace/{Package,CreatePackageRequest,UpdatePackageRequest,TemplateManifest,MarketplaceListing,MarketplaceSearchRequest}:category`), two `RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR[18]` entries, one D3 semantic entry `marketplace-category-retired` with non-empty reason and acceptance criteria, one `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment, the `[RETIRED]` rows in `authorable-surface/marketplace.json`, the deliberate `json-schema.manifest` deletion, the `renamed-defs.ts` note, the ADR-0122 pin count moved 837→841 (+6 −2), and the liveness row with the REMOVED note. The prescription (`retiredCategoryGuidance`) opens with the fully qualified key, names `businessFunctions`, `industries`, `solutionType` and `LEGACY_CATEGORY_MAPPING`, and carries no `os migrate meta` sentence — correct, since no conversion covers the surface. `facets.categories` is a nested response key, not an authorable-surface row, so no registry entry is owed for it; its parse refusal is pinned. The changeset carries the BREAKING banner, the FROM→TO remedy and the `adr-0087: registered` marker.
4. **"No D2 conversion" — true.** `os migrate meta` replays the chain over the loaded stack (`normalizeStackInput`); Package, the two requests, MarketplaceListing and MarketplaceSearchRequest are catalog rows and HTTP bodies, and `objectstack.manifest.json` is a file beside `objectstack.config.ts` that no stack loader reads. The precedents cited (`marketplace/PackageDependency:optional`, `kernel/PackageDependencyResolutionResult:resolvedIn`) are the same class. Pinned: `ALL_CONVERSIONS` holds no entry touching the family.
5. **Nothing at boot reads the retired keys — right; one runtime reader to route.** Readers of `objectstack.manifest.json` at the head: `os package publish`, `os deploy` (no `category` read), create-objectstack, the scenario exporter, `check:template-manifests`, `sync-template-versions.mjs` — none at boot. No runtime package imports the six schemas except the CLI. One runtime, non-boot reader of a `category` **wire field** exists in this repo and is not disclosed: `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-proxy-plugin.ts:437,466-480` filters the public R2 list snapshot by `?category=` against `r.category`. It parses no spec schema and no in-repo caller sends the parameter (`MarketplacePage.tsx:407` calls `listMarketplacePackages({ limit: 100 })` and filters client-side), so no boot-time tolerance is owed and nothing breaks at this head; but when cloud#3661 drops `category` from the snapshot the filter goes silently dead and the proxy needs the facet parameters. **Should-fix (disclosure and routing):** name it on cloud#3661's R2/Worker item or on #31011; no change to this PR.
6. **CLI refusal before any network call — right.** `run()` reads the artifact and the manifest from disk, then refuses at publish.ts:655-668 (`flags.category`, then `m.category`, then `readPublishTaxonomy`); `resolveCloudCredential` (local config) is at :731, the first network call `resolveInstallTarget` at :752 and the publish `fetch` at :1066. The message names the facets for the held value through `LEGACY_CATEGORY_MAPPING` (mapped → the functions and type; manual → the type and "yours to choose" with the 11 functions; unlistable → the reason; unknown → the 11 functions; `starter` → "never classified your package"). Pinned in `package-publish-taxonomy.test.ts` with `fetch` stubbed to count calls.
7. **Cross-check — correct and not over-strict.** `explainSolutionTypeContradiction`: `template` needs `unmanaged` in `resolveInstallModes(artifact.manifest)` (ADR-0131 D6; absent → `['managed']`), `connector` needs at least one entry in `artifact.connectors`, `app` or absent asks nothing. A package permitting both modes passes as a template; a connector that also ships objects passes; nothing forces a function onto a connector (the ruling leaves it to the author). The CLI reads the modes through `ManifestSchema.shape.installModes.safeParse`, so an unreadable value counts as the default rather than crashing (pinned). The three connector listing tests run the same rule against `stack.manifest` / `stack.connectors`.
8. **Blank template declares no facet — right.** `create-objectstack` copies `objectstack.manifest.json` into every scaffolded project (`rewrite-identity.ts`), so a facet there would classify apps it does not describe; `solutionType: template` would be refused by the cross-check, since the blank config declares no `installModes` (→ `['managed']`). §3.3 is labelled 方案/供参考, not a ruled decision. The consequence — a project scaffolded from blank is refused at marketplace submission until its author declares a function — is the ruling's own "never a catch-all". (The same file still ships `isStarter: true`, copied the same way; recorded `dead` in the ledger, out of this card's scope.)

### ② Semver level

- A narrowing at `minor` is what this spec line requires, not merely allows: AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3 ("a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves"; `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and carries the banner and the ADR-0087 disposition), ADR-0087's 2026-09-13 level amendment (#18003: pre-GA a metadata-facing retirement ships `minor`; an npm `major` is a planned act, never a side effect of one retirement), and `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (refuses `major` in the launch window). `Check Changeset` is green on this head.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is right: a tombstoned authorable key is `narrowed`; the new keys are `added`; several ⇒ `narrowed` over `added`. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the matching arm. The changeset grades `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/cli` `minor` and `create-objectstack` `patch` (it moves a template file, no protocol surface) — consistent with the gate's level axis.
- The guidance dates the removal "@objectstack/spec 18": the npm and protocol majors coincide at 18.x here (spec at 18.3.0; the retirement ships in the next minor), and the spelling matches the other `18` tombstones at the head, so ADR-0087's "names the npm release, never the protocol major" is not violated.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **(a) Release order (「等 cloud 上线再发 CLI（推荐）」) — purely the maintainer's release hold; nothing in this PR needs to carry it.** The ruling's step 1 says landing is not held; the hold sits on the `chore: version packages` PR. The changeset is the CHANGELOG an upgrading agent greps and should describe the contract, which it does; a deployment sequence written into it would be stale the day the hold lifts. The handbook already tells an author that a declared facet "is accepted and not yet shown" until each side adopts. No change.
- **(b) hotcrm's `category: crm` — disclosed, routed by the ruling, not yet filed.** The PR body ("Not touched: HotCRM's manifest (hotcrm lane)") and both os-dev reports ("carrier: hotcrm lane · noted, not filed") disclose it; ruling §6 item 8 assigns it to the hotcrm lane. No hotcrm card exists. **Escalate to the seat (should-fix, outside this PR):** file the hotcrm card before the CLI release the maintainer holds — the hold is the window. Not verified at hotcrm (not an input of this review).
- **(c) `template_manifest` keys recorded `dead`, not retired — right for this PR; the worklist is owed a card.** The ledger's discipline (spec-property-retirement §2) is that a `dead` row with `verifiedAt` and a note IS the ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove worklist; enrolling a new type measures its whole shape, and retiring seven unrelated keys (`name`, `specVersion`, `skills`, `scaffold` + 2 children, `visibility`, `publisher`, `isStarter`) in a taxonomy PR would be scope creep. `Spec property liveness` is green. **Escalate (should-fix, outside this PR):** the seat files one ADR-0049 card for the seven non-category `dead` rows; the dev's "carrier: none · noted, not filed" leaves them with no owner.
- **(d) cloud#3661 carry-overs found while judging ① (should-fix, carried there):** (i) a value outside `LEGACY_CATEGORY_MAPPING` reads `undefined` — treat as manual + original value as tag, never skip; (ii) the `integrations` rows' "read the manifest's original category first" is a migration step, not a table row; (iii) `MarketplaceListing.businessFunctions` is required, so the catalog must say what it serves for an already-approved row whose functions are still `manual` after the dry-run (complete it or withhold it from listings) — the cloud body's "Expected" does not yet name this.

### ④ Design judgment

- **Duplicates / out-of-order.** Duplicates are refused on every schema by the shared `distinct` refinement (spec, the CLI through `CreatePackageRequestSchema.shape`, scenario cards through `BusinessFunctionsSchema`), pinned in three suites. Order is the author's statement — the first value is the primary one by definition, and the gallery exporter reads `[0]` — so "out of order" is not a schema-detectable state; the handbook and the module doc say which comes first. One honest gap, recorded by the PR itself: `distinct` is a `.refine()` and does not project to JSON Schema (eight new `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` rows), so an author validating against the published `$schema` learns of a duplicate only at parse. A `uniqueItems` arm in `shared/refinement-projection.ts` would close it; the baseline makes that a public-contract decision, so it is a follow-up, not this PR. Should-fix (follow-up).
- **A connector re-tag that drops its function.** Not reachable through the contract: `solutionType` and `businessFunctions` are independent keys, the mapping writes `manual` (no function) for every integrations spelling instead of inventing one, `UpdatePackageRequest` carries no default so an omitted key leaves the stored functions alone, and the three connector manifests keep theirs (`[finance]`, `[it]`, `[collaboration, legal]`). The place a function was lost before — cloud's `publish-connector-apps.mjs` rewriting category — is cloud#3661 item 5, as the ruling assigns.
- **Search facet semantics.** The request declares array filters per facet (`businessFunctions`, `industries`, `solutionTypes`) and a scalar `maturity`, and states OR-inside / AND-across in the schema doc and the module header — the same sentence as ruling §2 总则. The spec can state it, not apply it; the catalog (cloud#3661 item 4) and the console (#31011) are named as the appliers. Consistent; no finding.
- **i18n keyed from `.options`.** `MarketplaceBusinessFunctionSchema.options` resolves through the `lazySchema` proxy (the CLI already lists the functions from it, tested). Keys are the kebab-case values (`marketplace.businessFunction.customer-service`), which i18next accepts; #31011's parity test iterating `.options` is the right guard, and `maturity` needs only `beta`. No finding.
- **A future enum value.** Appending a value is `Metadata-protocol: added` ⇒ `Clause-②: yes (widening)` at `minor` (AGENTS.md); renaming or removing one is an ADR-0087 narrowing. The module header states append-only, demand-pull (a real listed package or a ruled card) and "the console's labels in the same change" — and since `Type Check UI` / `Test UI` compile `ui/` against the PR's spec, a value without its nine labels reds its own PR once #31011's parity test exists. Right.

Findings, by weight: **must-fix: none.** Should-fix: ①5 route the `marketplace-proxy-plugin.ts` `?category=` filter; ③(b) file the hotcrm card; ③(c) file the ADR-0049 card for the seven `dead` rows; ③(d) three cloud#3661 carry-overs; ④ the `uniqueItems` projection follow-up. None changes this diff.
